newsitem.title: INDIA: Low caste party sees victory in Indian state poll.
newsitem.headline: Low caste party sees victory in Indian state poll.

text.p: A party representing the lowest Hindu castes predicted on Thursday it would win local polls in India's most populous state that are regarded as crucial for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government.

"We are heading for an outright victory to upset everyone's calculations," former Uttar Pradesh chief minister Mayawati told Reuters after the state on Thursday began the second phase of three-stage assembly elections.
In the state capital of Lucknow, voters queued up early to cast ballots.
With a population of 140 million people, Uttar Pradesh is a more populous than Japan or Pakistan.

Mayawati said her Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), representing the Dalits, or former Hindu untouchables, would sweep the polls with the Congress party of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao as its junior partner.

Her prediction was at odds with recent opinion polls that have given an edge to the rightist Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), India's main opposition group that has made Uttar Pradesh its main base.

The government cancelled four of the 164 races in the fray on Thursday, three of them due to violence. Those elections will be held on October 9, two days after the scheduled final phase of the polls.
Tens of thousands of paramilitary troops have been deployed to guard the elections that began on Monday in the state.
Police last week clamped an around-the-clock curfew on the Moslem-majority old quarter of Lucknow, the state capital and the main base of the BJP.

The polls have Deve Gowda's fractious United Front taking on the Congress party, which backs his minority government in New Delhi but is allied with the BSP in Uttar Pradesh, and the BJP in a three-way battle for the state's 425-seat lower house.

Politicians said the polls, in which 90 million people are eligible to vote, would test Deve Gowda's ability to overcome a challenge by the BJP, India's main opposition group and which is campaigning for mid-term parliamentary polls.

The BJP's campaign to build a Hindu temple at the site of a 16th century mosque in Uttar Pradesh catapulted it to power in several north Indian states and made it the main opposition party in parliament in 1991.

Analysts say the state, once a Congress bastion, could boost a recent trend of coalition politics that helped Deve Gowda form a minority government in June. Congress has ruled India for all but four years since independence in 1947.
